$comment: Negative syntax tests accepted by the grammar. See docs/conformance.md.
Each entry describes a constraint the current parser does not enforce.
Tests fail for unlisted mismatches, stale entries, and unknown case names.
Review the cause of each mismatch before changing this list.

sparql11-query.test_43: GROUP BY with SELECT * — a scoping rule over the whole query, not a shape.
sparql11-query.test_44: A projected variable not in the GROUP BY — scoping.
sparql11-query.test_45: The same alias bound twice in a projection — requires comparing two bindings.
sparql11-query.test_60: BIND scoping: the bound variable is already in scope.
sparql11-query.test_bad_values_too_few: VALUES row shorter than its variable list — an arity count, not a shape.
sparql11-query.test_bad_values_too_many: VALUES row longer than its variable list — as above.
sparql11-query.test_codepoint_invalid_escaped_bad_06: An escape naming an invalid code point: needs code-point arithmetic.

sparql11-update.test_43: A variable in DELETE DATA. The 1.1 grammar reaches this through TriplesTemplate; the prohibition is a separate constraint in the spec text.
sparql11-update.test_44: A variable in INSERT DATA, as above.
sparql11-update.test_50: A blank node in DELETE WHERE — a constraint in the spec text, not in the grammar.
sparql11-update.test_51: A blank node in a DELETE template, as above.
sparql11-update.test_52: A blank node in DELETE DATA, as above.
sparql11-update.test_54: The same blank-node label reused across two operations in a sequence — requires tracking labels between operations.

sparql12-syntax.duplicated-values-variable: The same variable twice in a VALUES list — requires comparing the list to itself.
sparql12-syntax.nested-aggregate-functions: An aggregate inside an aggregate — the grammar's Expression is uniform, and forbidding this needs to know where an aggregate already is.

sparql12-codepoint-escapes.surrogate-esc-01-bad: Lone or misordered surrogate escapes: needs code-point arithmetic across two UCHARs.

sparql12-triple-terms-negative.annotated-reifier-path: An annotation on an object reached through a property path. The current grammar does not enforce this restriction; see docs/conformance.md.
sparql12-triple-terms-negative.nested-annotated-path-anonreifier: As above, with the path inside an annotation block.
sparql12-triple-terms-negative.annotated-reifier-oneOrMore: As above (`+` path modifier). Passed before only because `+` failed to lex as a path modifier at all, so the file errored for the wrong reason.
sparql12-triple-terms-negative.annotated-anonreifier-oneOrMore: As above (`+` path modifier), and as above about why it used to pass.
